{"grade": 6, "complete": true, "main_gap": "Stated mark positions (2^j·delta) contradict the intended interval lengths in (9); correct marks are (2^j−1)·delta. Construction otherwise unambiguous.", "errors": [{"description": "Liu's construction: the marks that produce interval lengths δ,2δ,…,2^nδ are the partial sums (2^j−1)δ, not 2^jδ. Taken literally, the stated marks give lengths 2δ,2δ,3δ for n=2, which has coinciding subset sums (Γ=0) and destroys the lower bound. Repairable typo, since (9) fixes the intended partition and only (9) is used afterwards.", "quote": "Thus his marks are \(2^j\delta\) for \(1\le j\le n\), all distinct and
strictly inside the stick."}, {"description": "In the tree-component argument the crucial bookkeeping is compressed: it is not stated that every final piece lying in an interval of the chosen component belongs to a pair whose edge is inside that component (so that exactly the v_T−1 edge terms plus possibly x_r appear). The step is true but left implicit.", "quote": "Expanding each \(a_i\) as the sum of its descendant final pieces, every paired edge in the chosen component contributes, up to sign,
\(x_{2j-1}-x_{2j}\)."}, {"description": "The 56-unit 'grid example' is claimed to agree with the theorem, but with lengths (7,14,35) one has Γ=7/56 < 8/56, so the exhibited Xiang play is not optimal and the example does not illustrate the value 4/7. Harmless (explicitly labelled non-proof evidence) but misleading.", "quote": "Sorting gives Liu
\((18+13+1)/56=32/56=4/7\), in agreement with the theorem."}], "notes": "Answer 2^n/(2^{n+1}−1) is supported by a correct greedy-drafting lemma, a valid graph/bipartition lower bound (verified for parities, loops, fewer cuts) and a valid overlay construction with ≤ q−1 cuts, plus the subset-sum pigeonhole. Section 5 is extraneous."}
